texts.preamble: Sultan Singh Gora S/O Shri Gopi Ram Gora vs The Union Of India on 28 September, 2022
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioners argue that impugned gazette notification dated 01.10.2018 notified in the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (Recruitment and Appointment) Regulations, 2018, in so far as it prescribes minimum eligibility criteria and qualification for the appointment to the post of Food Safety Officer and notification dated 25.07.2018 amending Rajasthan Medical and Health Sub- Ordinate Rules, 1956, amending eligibility criteria for appointment to the post of Food Safety Officer is arbitrary and illegal. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that earlier there was a post of Food Inspector provided under the Rajasthan Medical and Health Sub-Ordinate Rules, 1956 and the minimum eligibility qualification prescribed for the said post included Bachelor in Pharmacy and Masters Degree in Pharmacy also. However, when amendment was carried out in the said rules, the authorities have now provided for creation of the post of Food Safety Officer with (3 of 4) [CW-10783/2022] eligibility qualifications which do not include B. Pharmacy, M. Pharmacy. He would submit that the nature of duty and functions required to be performed by the Food Inspector in the past and that of the Food Safety Officer is almost one and the same, except change in designation. Earlier the qualification in B. Pharmacy/M. Pharmacy was included as one of the eligibility qualification for appointment to the post of Food Inspector, therefore, merely because nomenclature has changed from Food Inspector to Food Safety Officer, exclusion of those possessed of B. Pharmacy/M. Pharmacy degree is per se arbitrary and illegal. His next submission is that in any case even according to the impugned rules and regulations, other equivalent/recognised qualifications are also treated as part of the eligibility criteria, the qualification possessed by the Sultan Singh Gora S/O Shri Gopi Ram Gora vs The Union Of India on 28 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172766806/ 2 petitioners are to be treated as equivalent to the eligibility qualification already prescribed under the relevant rules and regulations. After hearing learned counsel for the petitioners and going through the records of the case, particularly the notifications which have been impugned in this petition, we find the challenge to the constitutionality and validity of the rules without any merit. There is nothing on record to substantiate the submission that the post of Food Inspector on the one hand and Food Safety Officer on the other hand, carry identical duties, functions, responsibilities, powers under the relevant enactments. It is apparent that under the new regime of law, post of Food Safety Officer has been created and its qualifications have been prescribed separately. The writ courts would not draw equivalence of two qualifications as that is essentially the function of the experts. The contention of learned counsel for the petitioners that qualification of B. Pharmacy/M. Pharmacy ought to be notified as equivalent qualification, also cannot be accepted because it is for the competent authority to draw equivalence and notify. The rules provide that the equivalent qualifications may be those as may be prescribed by the Central Government.
